item.title: Gujarat High Court Directs Fresh Inquiry Into Custodial Death – Says Earlier Probe “Perfunctory”
item.dc:creator: Law Trend
item.description: The Gujarat High Court has directed a fresh inquiry, holding that the earlier probe was perfunctory and ignored medical evidence. The Bench observed that the State owes a heightened duty of care to persons in its custody, and that a magisterial inquiry under the BNSS must examine the medical record, the custody register and the statements of independent witnesses before any conclusion is reached; it set a time limit of three months for the fresh inquiry and directed that the family be heard. The matter will be listed again after the report is filed.
